title: Adaptive slab hire cadence & price-gating prototype (Jul 2027)
body:
Purpose:
Quick simulation sheet + notes for an "adaptive slab" approach: small committed slabs + automated price-gating for burst demand. Goal is to show headcount ramp, unit economics, and price sensitivity under 3 demand shapes so product/sales can validate go/no-go for an experiment.

High-level assumptions (single-line):
- Base hosted token mix: 70% generation(short-form), 20% chat/long-form, 10% embeddings.
- Baseline token price (current list): $0.004 / 1k tokens generation-equivalent.
- Committed slab sizes considered: 25k, 100k, 500k slots (units = concurrent throughput-buckets).
- Burst price-gating increments: +15%, +35%, +70% (to throttle non-committed traffic).
- HC cost per FTE (loaded): Eng infra = $250k, Model Ops = $220k, Support/CS = $160k, SRE = $230k.
- GPU fixed capacity cost apportioned into slab cost line (included in slab unit pricing).

Simple headcount-phase matrix (quarterly cadence)
Columns: role | base FTE today | target q3-2026 | target q4-2026 | target q1-2027 | notes
Eng infra | 18 | 20 | 22 | 24 | focus autoscale/placement optimizations
Model Ops | 6 | 8 | 10 | 12 | quantization & variant inventory ops
SRE | 7 | 8 | 9 | 10 | SLA ops for Dedicated clients
Support/CS | 12 | 13 | 14 | 16 | onboarding and enterprise runbooks
Finance/RevOps | 4 | 4 | 5 | 5 | pricing instrumentation
Total FTE | 47 | 53 | 60 | 67 | incremental hiring phased by slab commitments

Monthly burn (run-rate) estimate by quarter (USD thousands)
Q3-2026: FTE comp 1,050; slab fixed costs 320; infra cloud 280; ops/tools 95; total 1,745
Q4-2026: FTE comp 1,190; slab fixed 380; infra cloud 330; ops/tools 110; total 2,010
Q1-2027: FTE comp 1,350; slab fixed 460; infra cloud 410; ops/tools 125; total 2,345

Pricing sensitivity scenarios (revenue / GP impact) - 3 demand shapes: 
- Shape A (steady-growth): +20% token volume q/q
- Shape B (peak-surge seasonal): +80% peak with 30% of traffic on burst windows
- Shape C (churny high variance): average stable but 2x spikes 5% of time

We model 3 price-gating policies:
Policy 0 (No gating) = baseline price, absorb overage as spot
Policy 1 (Soft gating) = +15% price during burst windows, preferential routing to slabs when available
Policy 2 (Hard gating) = +35% price during burst; non-compliant requests deferred/queued or rate-limited
Policy 3 (Aggressive gating) = +70% price in extreme high-load windows; fallback to smaller models allowed

Summary table (example rows; numbers rounded)
Scenario | Policy | Adj price /1k | Avg monthly tokens (B) | Revenue (k$/mo) | Gross margin % (est) | Notes
A | P0 | 0.0040 | 2.0 | 8,000 | 42% | baseline
A | P1 | 0.0046 | 2.0 | 9,200 | 47% | small upside from gating
A | P2 | 0.0054 | 2.0 | 10,800 | 52% | higher margin, potential churn risk
B | P0 | 0.0040 | 2.8 (peaks applied) | 11,200 | 36% | big variable infra costs reduce margin
B | P1 | 0.0046 | 2.6 (effective dampening) | 11,960 | 44% | gating shifts some burst revenue to committed slab pricing
B | P3 | 0.0068 | 2.2 (throttled demand) | 14,960 | 58% | revenue concentrated to committed customers; lower variable cost
C | P0 | 0.0040 | 2.05 | 8,200 | 40% | spikes eat margin
C | P2 | 0.0054 | 2.02 | 10,910 | 51% | slightly lower average volume but better margins

Headcount sensitivity by scenario: incremental hiring trigger rules
- If sustained 3-month rolling avg token volume > 25% above forecast: +2 Eng infra FTE and +1 Model Ops FTE (immediate hire).
- If peak windows exceed baseline slab capacity > 50% for more than 6 weeks: prioritize contract SRE + 1 permanent SRE.
- If enterprise committed slab bookings > $X (TBD): accelerate CS hire by +2 for onboarding.

Operational action checklist (short):
- [ ] Wire a simple meter in prod to tag burst-vs-committed traffic (JIRA OPS-2198).
- [ ] Add price-gating flag in pricing service (PR open: GH #1127).
- [ ] Run an A/B experiment for soft gating on 5% of traffic for 6 weeks (A/B design doc linked).
- [ ] Finance to build rolling 13-week liquidity view including gating sensitivity (owner: Asha).
- [ ] Draft customer comms template for gating windows (owner: Marisol)

Open questions / risks (notes):
- Elasticity unknown: will a +35% gating lead to reduced consumption or substitution to other providers? Need small-market experiments.
- Contract/legal: how to represent gating in TOS and SLA (escalation to legal team).
- Instrumentation latency: need near-real-time visibility into token mix to trigger gating correctly.
- Brand/CS risk: gating might be perceived poorly by mid-market customers; segment gating by tier.

Quick experiment plan (6 weeks):
Week 0: deploy metric tagging + price flag behind feature flag.
Week 1: run P1 gating on 5% non-enterprise traffic; collect elasticity signals.
Week 3: expand to 20% on lower-risk cohorts; measure churn and request latency.
Week 5: evaluate economics (run-rate margin delta, net new committed slab bookings).
Decision gate: pursue broader rollout if gating increases gross margin by >6pp with <1% uplift in churn.

Appendix (small tables)
Role loaded cost (USD) | FTE capex equivalent per month
Eng infra | 20,833
Model Ops | 18,333
SRE | 19,167
Support/CS | 13,333
Finance/RevOps | 10,000

Slab pricing sketch (per month, illustrative)
Slab size | monthly cost to Redwood | effective price-equivalent /1k tokens (assumes utilization 60%)
25k | 60k | 0.0036
100k | 200k | 0.0028
500k | 850k | 0.0022

Notes to reviewer: this is a working prototype sheet — numbers are deliberately conservative and rounded. Please comment inline with sensitivity runs you'd like added (e.g., incremental model-quantization uplift scenarios, parity pricing for Dedicated vs Hosted).
